lead.title: News live: NT chief minister wants more datacentres in the Territory; Greens urges national cabinet to refocus on gendered violence ‘before it’s too late’
lead.summary: Follow updates live Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Lia Finocchiaro , the chief minister of the Northern Territory, maintained the region should be able to “decide its energy policy and its energy mix” when it comes to datacentres, without rules imposed by the federal government. She told RN: Ultimately, we don’t need the federal government coming in heavy-handed and trying to dictate to states and territories how they should be developing datacentres or not and what energy mix they should be using. There is no question that the territory can handle datacentres and rapid investment as a result of the Beetaloo Basin. It will actually support and underpin economic growth that we are fighting desperately for. … I completely appreciate, particularly with the east coast energy crisis, that there are concerns about datacentres in southern states. But the Northern Territory has the answers to all of those problems. This is a big challenge and a big opportunity for Australia. If we lean back and miss the opportunity that has negative consequences for our economy, our productivity and our security. If we lean in and get this right as one country with one approach rather than eight different approaches, then that offers the opportunity to make sure that artificial intelligence and datacentres and AI training is harnessed here in the national interest in a coordinated and effective way that makes Australia stronger. These AI standards are all about making sure that Australia maximises the advantage, maximises the right kind of investment in the right places, and that delivers to support our ambitions to build a modern electricity system for Australia. Continue reading...

Sports.summary: After an unacceptable performance against Brentford, head coach still believes they can avoid sinking feeling this season What’s in a name? Quite a bit, judging by the discussion at Roberto De Zerbi’s Tottenham press conference on Tuesday, shortly after the club had completed the £75m signing of Savinho from Manchester City and the Brazil winger had let everybody know that he wanted to be called Sávio from now on. He will have that name on his Spurs shirt above his No 17, which he has taken over from Cristian Romero, the former captain who has moved to Atlético Madrid. The 22-year-old went by Sávio at various times before his two seasons at City but there was nonetheless speculation about the reasons for the reversion. Sports.title: Victor Torp seals Coventry’s Carabao Cup win at Plymouth in six-goal thriller
Sports.summary: A midweek trip to Devon always had the makings of a tricky trip for a Coventry team focused on Premier League survival. Such feelings quickly evaporated when Frank Lampard’s side raced into a two-goal lead with just four minutes and six seconds on the clock, Taiwo Awoniyi opening his account for his new club before Jack Rudoni doubled Coventry’s advantage. But, ultimately, Coventry were made to toil before chalking up a welcome first victory of the season. But Plymouth have form for a cup upset and another was brewing when Xavier Amaechi pulled Tom Cleverley’s side level nine minutes into the second half. Coventry, to their credit, roused once more, the substitute Ephron Mason-Clark regaining the lead before Victor Torp sealed progress to the Carabao Cup third round from the penalty spot. “You’ve got to enjoy a win, always,” Lampard said. “A win is a big deal because it’s a nice feeling to take back on the bus for four hours.” Continue reading...
